name: South Dakota
summary: Statutes, codified court rules (SDCL 15-6, 15-26A, 19-19, Title 23A) and ARSD rules are constructible per section from the LRC's server-rendered API pages (sdlegislature.gov/api/Statutes/{section}.html, /api/Rules/Rule/{rule}.html); the human /Statutes/ URLs are a JavaScript shell. The constitution is per-section on the same host but the script extracts 0 characters, so WebFetch plus Justia carry it. Supreme Court opinions (2006–, public-domain 'YYYY S.D. N' with ¶ pinpoints) are found by a GET party-name search on ujs.sd.gov and read as PDFs by fetch_doc.py (WebFetch is gated on them); Justia covers older years. Further review is SCOTUS certiorari only, findable by party name.

citation_map.notes: SDCL 15-26A-69.1: opinions released on or after Jan. 1, 1996 are cited 'YYYY S.D. N' with pinpoints to clerk-assigned ¶ numbers; earlier opinions by S.D. Reports (ended 1976, vol. 90 per memory) or N.W./N.W.2d. Court style and practitioners write both 'S.D.' and 'SD' ('2006 SD 113' appears in UJS listing titles). SDCL numbers are title-chapter-section with letters allowed (15-26A, 23A) and decimals (2-16-13.1); a '§§ 22-18-1 to -1.1' range is a span — take the first section. Court rules are codified: civil procedure = SDCL 15-6 (rule subsections are separate sections, e.g. 15-6-56(c)), evidence = 19-19 (FRE numbers), appellate = 15-26A, criminal = Title 23A (federal rule number only in the catchline). Bare 'Rule 56(c)' or 'Rule 702' is generic: route only with South Dakota context, then map to 15-6-56(c) / 19-19-702. Routing guards: 'S.D.' is also the Southern District abbreviation in federal cites ('S.D.N.Y.', 'S.D. Ohio'); the public-domain regex requires a 1996+ year directly before 'S.D.' and a number after, and the N.W. pattern requires '(S.D. YYYY)' or a parallel S.D. Reports cite, so federal district parentheticals do not route here. Bare N.W.2d cites, 'SL YYYY, ch N' and 5-digit docket numbers are context_required (N.W. also covers IA, MI, MN, NE, ND, WI). ARSD numbers use colons (67:16:01:01) and route only with an ARSD / S.D. Admin. R. prefix; register cites are 'NN SDR NNN'. CourtListener id 'sd' is from memory and unverified.

sources.title: South Dakota Codified Laws (LRC per-section HTML API)
sources.publisher: South Dakota Legislative Research Council (Code Commission)
sources.official_status_evidence: SDCL 2-16-13 (read at https://sdlegislature.gov/api/Statutes/2-16-13.html) defines the official code as the printed revised volumes and supplements; 2-16-13.1 excludes catchlines, notes and appendices. No statement found that the online text is official, and no UELMA authentication.
sources.coverage: All titles of the SDCL, including the court rules codified in it (15-6 civil procedure, 15-26A appellate, 19-19 evidence, Title 23A criminal procedure) and chapter appendices (e.g. 16-18-A Rules of Professional Conduct). Section pages carry the 'Source:' history note.

access.pattern_rules: {section} is the SDCL number exactly as cited, hyphens kept, no padding: 22-18-1, 53-1-1, 32-23-1, 19-19-702, 15-26A-60, 23A-8-3, 2-16-13.1. Chapter keys (22-18) and title keys (22) return the chapter's or title's table of contents; append ?all=true to a chapter key to get every section's text on one page (22-18.html?all=true = 21,832 chars). Rule subsections that are separate SDCL sections keep their parenthetical: 15-6-56(c), 15-6-12(b) (literal parentheses in the URL). The bare parent 15-6-56.html returns HTTP 200 with 0 characters: if a page comes back empty, re-try with the citation's first parenthetical letter, never guess further. Constitution sections are NOT served here (see sd-constitution-lrc). The human-facing https://sdlegislature.gov/Statutes/{section} is a Vue app: both fetch routes get only 'Your browser is not supported'. JSON variant: https://sdlegislature.gov/api/Statutes/Statute/{section} (Html field plus Previous/Next/parents).
access.navigation: Only if a section key fails: title page /api/Statutes/22.html (chapter list, no section ranges) → chapter page /api/Statutes/22-18.html lists every section number and catchline with links of the form https://sdlegislature.gov/Statutes?Statute=22-18-1 → take the number and use the url_pattern.

automation.robots_txt: User-agent: * — Disallow only /Edge-logo.svg, /Firefox-logo., /chrome-logo.svg, /Unsupported.js, /pdfviewer, /PDFViewer; /api/ paths allowed. Sitemaps: /Statutes.xml, /Rules.xml, /api/Documents/Index/Sitemap.xml
automation.notes: The /api/Statutes/{section}.html pages are plain server-rendered HTML (no JS). WebFetch on the built URL /api/Statutes/53-1-1.html went through without an approval prompt. Sitemaps https://sdlegislature.gov/Statutes.1.xml and .2.xml (2.6M chars) list every section URL with a lastmod date.

currency.where: None on section pages. The SPA reads https://sdlegislature.gov/api/Statutes/LastStatuesEffectiveDate (sic) for its 'Last Updated' label; the sitemap index shows the same date.

hazards: the human /Statutes/{section} URL is a JavaScript shell for both fetch routes; always use /api/Statutes/{section}.html
rule-numbered sections in 15-6 need the parenthetical (15-6-56(c)); the bare number gives an empty 200 page, not a 404
unknown keys also give an empty 200 page, not a 404: treat 0 characters as not found
no currency line on the page itself

sources.title: South Dakota Supreme Court opinions (UJS)
sources.official_status_evidence: Slip opinions issued by the Court carrying the clerk-assigned public-domain citation ('2026 S.D. 48'), which SDCL 15-26A-69.1 makes the required citation form from 1996.
sources.coverage: Supreme Court opinions 2006–present on the site (year filter 2006–2026; year=1996 archive=true returns 0). South Dakota has no intermediate appellate court.

access.pattern_rules: Plain GET. keywords matches the case TITLE only (party names): docket numbers (31307) and citation strings ('2010 S.D. 105') do not match. Always add archive=true — older opinions (and some 2026 ones) are 'archived' and hidden otherwise. Each row: date, 'STATE v. LUCERO, 2026 S.D. 48', sequence number; the PDF is https://ujs.sd.gov/media/{random}/{docket}.pdf — the random segment is not constructible, take the link from the listing (fetch_doc.py links … pdf). The docket number is the PDF file name.

script_candidates.why: GET /api/Statutes/Statute/{section} returns JSON (Html, CatchLine, Previous/Next, parents); /api/Statutes/{section}.html plain HTML; /api/Statutes/LastStatuesEffectiveDate gives currency; sitemaps /Statutes.1.xml and /Statutes.2.xml list every section and constitution URL with lastmod — a complete deterministic resolver and change detector.
